observation_summary: The ExtendedMessageFormat class enters an infinite loop when parsing patterns containing single quotes, leading to an OutOfMemoryError.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect algorithmic step in the `appendQuotedString` method. When an escaped quote is encountered, the parser fails to advance the `ParsePosition` index. This causes the loop to repeatedly process the same character, resulting in an infinite loop and eventual memory exhaustion. Adding a call to `next(pos)` to advance the index is a procedural correction to the parsing algorithm.
evidence_used: The bug report description explicitly identifies the fix as adding 'next(pos)' to advance the parse position.
The stack trace shows the failure occurs within the `appendQuotedString` method.
The code snippet at line 422 shows the logic that handles the quote character without advancing the position.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a call, it is not a guard or validation check; it is a necessary step in the iteration logic of the parsing algorithm.
